question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x+1) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-5) \\ 3x+1 & =x-5 \\ 2x & =-6 \\ x & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=-3$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x+1) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-5) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(3(-3)+1) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-3-5) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(-8) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-8)\end{aligned}
$$

However, $\operatorname{ln}⁡(-8)$ is not a real number.

Therefore, we conclude that the equation has no real solutions.
